state.product: MenteViva, iOS exercise app for older adults. Warm, no-fail, big-target design, EN+ES, offline, zero third-party dependencies, solo developer. Copy ceiling: 'fun mental exercise', no medical claims. Points were removed from the UI because players found them confusing. Each device holds one person's play history; the owner plays on an iPhone and the primary player on his own iPad.
state.player: Primary player: an older adult who plays alone on his own iPad. The owner, his adult child, also plays on a separate device and wants to track his own progress too. The owner does not want the app to feel like supervision of either of them.
state.games: Memory Lane (pair matching, 4/6/8 pairs, can use the family's own photos), Name the Herd (pick the items of a category), Quick Eyes (an item flashes, find it among 4), Color Clash (Stroop), Number Trail (addition streaks). Each session stores accuracy, rounds, duration and difficulty level.
state.playtest_findings: Memory Lane, Name the Herd and Quick Eyes held his attention; Color Clash and Number Trail fell flat. He recognizes familiar faces but cannot recall the name: the missing piece is the name or a short phrase tied to a photo (a person, a nickname, a place such as a family home, an event such as an anniversary).
state.owner_decisions: Proposed, not yet decided: (1) photos get an optional short caption typed by family, kept on the device only; (2) a photo-reminiscence game where he sees a photo, is asked 'Who is this?', and taps 'Show me' to reveal and hear the caption, no wrong answer, with bundled everyday objects when there are no photos; (3) a Memory Lane variant matching a photo to its caption; (4) Number Trail gains subtraction, multiplication and exact division as difficulty steps; (5) My Week becomes one row per day with a count per game instead of one row per session; (6) progress is measured with rates, never sums: mean accuracy per play, level reached, days played per week, trends shown only after 3+ plays and compared only to the player's own earlier weeks; (7) the 'For family' screen is renamed to a per-device 'My progress' and shows the same rates to whoever holds the device, while hiding games and pinning difficulty move to a separate 'Set up'.
state.gamification_candidates: week_ring: 7 dots per week, one filled per day played, no loss state. streak: consecutive days played, resets to zero on a miss. weekly_count_only: a plain count of days played this week. personal_bests: best week so far, compared only to oneself. milestones: one-time warm messages such as first time reaching Hard. challenge_level: an opt-in level above Hard, off by default. Ruled out by the owner: leaderboards, pressure timers, reminder notifications.

consistency_display.instructions: Which single view of consistency best motivates this player and his adult child without guilt?

criteria.week_ring: A ring of 7 dots per week, a dot filled for each day played, never a loss state
criteria.streak: A count of consecutive days played that resets to zero after a missed day
criteria.weekly_count_only: A plain count of days played this week, no visual

progress_screen_framing.instructions: How should the screen with rates and trends be framed?

criteria.my_progress_per_device: A per-device 'My progress' showing the same rates to whoever holds the device, with hide-games and pin-difficulty moved to a separate 'Set up'
criteria.keep_family_screen: Keep the caregiver-oriented 'For family' screen as it is
criteria.separate_caregiver_view: Two views: a warm player view and a numbers view labeled for caregivers

build_order_after_captions.instructions: After photo captions exist, which should be built first?

criteria.photo_caption_reminiscence: The photo-reminiscence game: photo, 'Who is this?', tap to reveal and hear the caption
criteria.memory_lane_name_match: Memory Lane variant: match a photo to its caption
criteria.number_trail_operators: Number Trail with subtraction, multiplication and division as difficulty steps
criteria.my_week_and_progress: The per-day counts in My Week and the per-device My progress screen

captions_before_games.instructions: Should photo captions be built as their own foundation before any game uses them?

criteria.true: Both the reminiscence game and the Memory Lane variant need captions, and the caption field is also the privacy-sensitive part; ship it alone first
criteria.false: Build the reminiscence game with captions inside it; a separate foundation delays visible value

my_week_per_day_counts.instructions: Should My Week show one row per day with a count per game, replacing one row per session?

criteria.true: Seven short rows instead of an ever-growing log reads as progress, not as a record of everything
criteria.false: The per-session list is concrete and warm; a count loses the sense of each time he played

show_game_mix.instructions: Should the progress screen show the share of this week's plays per game (for example 50% one game, 0% another)?

criteria.true: It shows which games resonate and which are ignored, labeled 'played this week' not 'favorite'
criteria.false: The share mostly reflects what the daily plan suggested, so it can mislead until games are chosen by hand

challenge_level.instructions: Should an opt-in level above Hard exist, off by default and never shown to the primary player unless turned on?

criteria.true: The owner wants a challenge for himself and the app serves two players
criteria.false: A level only one person uses adds code and settings for one user; wait for a request

number_trail_operators_by_level.instructions: Should Number Trail add subtraction (never below zero), then multiplication and exact division, as difficulty steps rather than a random mix?

criteria.true: Operators map cleanly onto the existing easy/medium/hard ladder and keep each level predictable
criteria.false: A random mix keeps the game less predictable and engaging for players who find it flat
